links.comparator_used: Baseline LLM without retrieval (C0), compared with RAG over raw clinical text (C1)
links.effect: Unsupported claims rose from 5.0% (95% CI: 3.8–6.4%) at baseline to 43.6% (95% CI: 40.1–47.2%) with RAG, an 8.7-fold increase (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.31)
links.tradeoff: RAG added a new failure mode: sharply more unsupported claims than the baseline LLM.
links.quote: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, RAG increases rather than decreases hallucination in clinical text generation.

links.effect: Structured artifacts in single-pass generation gave 8.4% (95% CI: 6.7–10.3%) unsupported claims, versus 43.6% (95% CI: 40.1–47.2%) with RAG over raw clinical text
links.quote: Structured representation with explicit provenance offers a more effective approach to grounding LLM outputs in verifiable patient data.

links.outcome: Unsupported claims, contraindication miss rate, clinician utility
links.effect: Agent workflow had 21.1% unsupported claims, with the lowest contraindication miss rate (0.04) and the highest clinician utility scores; single-pass artifact generation had 8.4% unsupported claims
links.tradeoff: Unsupported claim rate (21.1%) was higher than in single-pass artifact generation (8.4%).
links.quote: The agent workflow achieved 21.1% unsupported claims with the lowest contraindication miss rate (0.04) and highest clinician utility scores.

links.comparator_used: Ablation of the citation requirement from the artifact-based system
links.effect: Citation requirements contributed most to safety improvements in the ablation analysis; no numbers given in the abstract
links.quote: Ablation analysis revealed that citation requirements and constraint checking contributed most to safety improvements.

design_hint: retrieval grounding vs structured artifact representation and agentic verification guardrails
